message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What You Need | How It Works | |---------|---------------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever house rule you set). | Points are earned by being the first to empty your hand in each round. The winner of the round gets points equal to the total value of all cards left in opponents’ hands. | | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (Red, Green, Blue, Yellow) × 25 cards each + 8 Wild cards (4 + 4). | 4 × 25 = 100 + 8 Wild = 108. | | **Setup** | • Shuffle the deck.
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining deck face‑down as the draw pile.
• Turn the top card of the draw pile face‑up to start the discard pile. | If the first card is a special card (Skip, Reverse, Draw Two, or Wild), treat it as if it had been played by the dealer. | | **Card Types** | 1. **Number cards** (0–9).
2. **Action cards**: Skip, Reverse, Draw Two.
3. **Wild cards**: Wild, Wild Draw Four. | • Number cards match by color or number.
• Action cards match by color or same action.
• Wild cards match any color; the player who plays them chooses the new color. | | **Turn Order** | Clockwise, unless a Reverse card changes direction. | Reverse flips the direction; if only two players, Reverse acts like a Skip. | | **Playing a Card** | • On your turn, play one card that matches the top card in color, number, or action.
• If you have no playable card, you must draw one from the draw pile.
• If the drawn card is playable, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | If you cannot play after drawing, you must pass. | | **Special Cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – changes direction of play.
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and loses their turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – you choose the new color and the next player draws four cards. | *Wild Draw Four* can only be played if you have no other playable card. If challenged and you actually had a playable card, the challenger draws six cards instead of four. | | **Calling “UNO”** | When you have one card left, you must say “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. | If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a Round** | First player to discard all cards wins the round. | The winner scores points equal to the sum of all cards still held by opponents. | | **Winning the Game** | First player to reach the target score (usually 500) wins the game. | If you’re playing a shorter game, set a lower target or play a single round. | --- ### Quick Play‑by‑Play Example 1. **Dealer** deals 7 cards to each player. 2. **Top card** of the draw pile is a **Red 5** → discard pile starts with Red 5. 3. Player 1 (clockwise) has a **Red 9** → plays it. 4. Player 2 has a **Blue 9** → plays it. 5. Player 3 has a **Yellow 9** → plays it. 6. Player 4 has a **Green 9** → plays it. 7. Player 1 has a **Draw Two** → plays it. Player 2 draws two cards and skips. 8. Player 3 continues, etc. --- ### Common Variations & House Rules | Variation | What It Changes | |-----------|-----------------| | **Stacking** | Players can stack Draw Two or Wild Draw Four cards on top of each other, forcing the next player to draw the cumulative total unless they can stack again. | | **No Wild Draw Four Challenge** | Players cannot challenge Wild Draw Four; it’s always legal. | | **“Uno” Penalty** | Instead of drawing two cards, the penalty could be drawing four or even losing a turn. | | **“Skip” Penalty** | Some groups make a Skip card double‑skip (next two players lose turns). | | **“Reverse” for Two Players** | Reverse acts as a Skip (next player loses turn). | | **“Draw 5” or “Draw 10”** | Replace Draw Two with higher penalties for more excitement. | | **“Wild” Color Change** | Some players allow a Wild to change color to any color, even if the player has a matching color card. | Feel free to mix and match these variations to suit your group’s style!
